$Comment:
The sawmill's session-loyalty find table, referenced from the station's Bonus.Lootables. A Roll grants what ELSE a cycle handed over: how MUCH of the thing you made is the action's own Recipe.Yield plus its OutputItems rolls, and a find can only ever ADD something different, never multiply that. This table grants drop lists rather than output items because a find IS a different thing - life essence shaken loose from the milled logs, not more planks.

ONE roll lives here, and that is the pattern to copy. A Lootable folds by id and a later layer replaces the whole FILE, so a table holding a single roll is one a pack can re-tune by shipping its own copy, inheriting nothing else along with it. The Sawmill spreads its bonuses across three such tables: this loyalty ladder any worker can reach, SawmillTrophy for the Sawmiller's Hatchet chase, and SawmillMasterworkFinds for the fourth tier that chase pays out. Each is replaceable on its own.

Rolls.$Comment: Read left to right: Trigger Cycle evaluates once per completed milling cycle. Conditions gates the whole Roll on rpgstations:cycle_count 10 or higher, so the first nine cycles of a session never even roll - finds reward staying at the bench, not tapping it - AND on tool quality 2 or better, so a starter Wood or Crude hatchet mills its planks but never shakes a find loose; Iron-grade steel is where the finds begin. Chance then passes 15 percent of those cycles. Ladder sums its Factors (a FactorRef[] summed before the floor lookup; a single-factor ladder authors a one-element array) and takes the HIGHEST floor the sum reaches, never several: cycles 10 to 24 grant the T1 table, cycles 25 to 49 the T2 table, and cycle 50 onward the T3 table, the upper two each carrying the same coin sound and spark burst on their own floor Presentation (the loyalty ladder's cue is a steady one; the grander legendary fanfare is reserved for the trophy). The referenced tables are this jar's own Server/Drops assets, and each pays two things: OFFCUTS, pulled from the shared RPG_Station_Sawmill_Byproducts list (fibre, bark, sap, sticks - one pull at T1 and T2, two at T3), plus life essence from its own weighted Choice. T1 pays offcuts alone, so essence entering the table at all is what makes T2 a step up rather than more of the same; T2 adds a 20 percent chance of 1 to 3 essence, and T3 doubles the offcuts and makes essence near-certain (95 percent for 2 to 4, with a 2 percent jackpot of one concentrated). The deep tier nearly always pays on a winning roll because its scarcity is carried by this Roll's own 15 percent chance rather than by the table being stingy. A ten-minute session runs about 124 cycles, so at 15 percent a worker sees roughly 18 finds in a full session, and past cycle 50 the top tier covers well over half of them. Grants.DropLists is a plural array - a floor could roll a guaranteed common table plus a rare one as two independent entries, each rolled once through the native ItemModule.getRandomItemDrops. Floors resolve through the one shared ladder core every ladder in this schema uses: highest reached Min wins, a Min of 0 is reachable, and two floors sharing a Min is a validator warning because only the last authored one could ever grant. A floor's own celebration only plays when its referenced table actually paid, so the T2 coin chime and the T3 legendary fanfare stay silent on a cycle whose table resolved to its own empty entry rather than firing over an empty hand.
